📖 How to Read This Report

A plain-English guide to every metric, signal, and score used in this report.

Composite Score & Signals

COMPOSITE SCORE

Composite Score (0–100)

A single number combining all factors into one rating. Higher is better.

75–100 Strong Buy   60–74 Buy   45–59 Hold   30–44 Weak   0–29 Avoid

SCORING

How Scores Are Calculated

Each factor is percentile-ranked across all stocks (0–100). A score of 80 means better than 80% of the universe on that factor.

Extreme outliers are trimmed at the 5th/95th percentile. Missing data defaults to 50 (neutral).

CHANGE

Score Change Indicators

▲ and ▼ next to the score bar show the change vs the previous run.

↑ = signal upgraded (e.g. Hold → Buy). ↓ = signal downgraded.

Valuation

VALUATION

P/E Ratio

Price divided by earnings per share. Lower = cheaper relative to profits.

Negative P/E = loss-making company, excluded from scoring. Context matters — tech trades at higher P/Es than utilities.

VALUATION

Forward P/E

Same as P/E but uses forecast earnings for the next 12 months.

Forward P/E lower than trailing = earnings expected to grow. Higher = earnings expected to fall.

VALUATION

P/B & EV/EBITDA

P/B compares price to net asset value. Below 1.0 = trading below asset value.

EV/EBITDA is capital-structure-neutral. Below 10 = cheap, 10–15 = fair, above 20 = expensive.

VALUATION

Analyst Upside

% difference between current price and consensus analyst target.

+30% = analysts think the stock is worth 30% more. Targets are typically 12-month forecasts — treat with some scepticism.

Technical Indicators

TECHNICAL

Moving Averages (MA50 / MA200 / MA750)

Average closing price over 50, 200, or 750 (~3 years) trading days. Smooths out noise to show the underlying trend.

Price above MA = uptrend. Below MA = downtrend. MA750 is the long-term anchor.

TECHNICAL

Golden Cross

Occurs when the 50-day MA crosses above the 200-day MA.

Bullish signal — short-term momentum strengthening vs long-term trend. Often used as a buy trigger by institutional investors.

TECHNICAL

Death Cross

Occurs when the 50-day MA crosses below the 200-day MA.

Bearish signal — short-term momentum weakening. Can indicate the start of a prolonged downtrend.

TECHNICAL

Momentum (1M / 3M / 6M / 12M)

% price return over each period. Stocks that have performed well recently tend to continue outperforming short-term.

Positive across all timeframes = strong trend. Negative across all = persistent weakness.

TECHNICAL

90-Day Sparkline

A miniature price chart showing the last 90 trading days of price movement.

Green line = price is higher now than 90 days ago. Red line = lower.

TECHNICAL

52-Week Range %

Where the current price sits within its 52-week high-low range.

100% = at the 52-week high. 0% = at the 52-week low.

Risk

RISK

Beta

How much the stock moves relative to the market. 1.0 = in line with market. 1.5 = 50% more volatile. 0.5 = half as volatile.

High-beta amplifies gains in bull markets but amplifies losses in bear markets.

RISK

Short Interest %

% of shares sold short — investors betting the price will fall.

Above 10% = significant bearish sentiment. Very high short interest can also trigger a short squeeze if the price rises.

RISK

Beta-Adjusted Upside

Analyst upside divided by beta. Rewards high upside without excessive market risk.

A stock with 30% upside and beta 0.8 scores better than one with 30% upside and beta 2.0.

Financial Health

FINANCIAL HEALTH

Piotroski F-Score (0–9)

A 9-point financial health checklist covering profitability, leverage, and efficiency. Each criterion scores 1 if met.

7–9 = strong   4–6 = average   0–3 = weak (flagged with ⚠)

FINANCIAL HEALTH

Earnings Surprise

How much the most recent earnings beat or missed analyst estimates.

Positive = beat estimates, often triggers a price rise. Negative = missed, often triggers a sell-off.

FINANCIAL HEALTH

Dividend Yield & Ex-Div Date

Annual dividend as % of share price. Higher = more income, but yields above 8–10% may signal a dividend cut risk.

Ex-Div Date = the date you must hold the stock by to receive the next dividend payment.

FINANCIAL HEALTH

Revenue Growth

Year-on-year % change in total revenue. Consistent positive growth = healthy business.

Declining revenue can signal structural problems even if profits are currently healthy.

Stock Splits

SPLITS

Stock Splits (since 2000)

A stock split increases the number of shares while reducing the price proportionally. A 4:1 split means each share becomes 4 shares at 1/4 the price.

Frequent splits (e.g. Apple, Nvidia) are often a sign of long-term price appreciation — a company only splits when the price has risen significantly.

Hover over the Splits cell in the screener to see the individual split dates and ratios.

SPLITS

Average Split Ratio

The average ratio across all splits since 2000. A ratio of 4.0 means shares were typically split 4-for-1.

A stock with 3 splits averaging 3:1 has multiplied its share count ~27x since 2000 — implying very strong long-term price growth.

Market Analysis

MARKET

Market Breadth

% of major indices in an uptrend (price above 200-day MA).

Bullish = 60%+ in uptrend. Neutral = 40–60%. Bearish = below 40%.

MARKET

Sector Rotation

Tracks which sectors are gaining or losing money. Shows where investors are moving capital.

Risk-on: money flows into Technology, Consumer Discretionary, Financials. Risk-off: flows into Utilities, Healthcare, Consumer Staples.

MARKET

VIX — Fear Gauge

Expected market volatility over the next 30 days based on S&P 500 options.

Below 15 = calm. 15–20 = normal. 20–30 = elevated. 30–40 = high stress. Above 40 = extreme fear.

MARKET

Watchlist

Add tickers (one per line) to Outputs/watchlist.txt to highlight them in the report.

Watchlist stocks appear with a ★ star, are highlighted in yellow, and get their own dedicated tab.
